chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Umar ibn Abdul Aziz, from Ahmad ibn Abu Dawood, from Abdullah ibn Abdul Rahman, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

He said to me: 'Shall I teach you a supplication you can supplicate with, which we, the People of the Household, use whenever a matter worries us and we fear from the ruling authorities a matter we cannot face with, we supplicate with it?' I said, 'Yes, may my father and my mother be (sacrificed) for you, O son of the Messenger of Allah!'

He said: 'Say, O the One who existed before everything, and O the One Who Brought everything into being, and O the One Who would be Remaining after everything! Send Salawāt upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, and Do for me such and such.'

key_terms.لَا قِبَلَ لَنَا بِهِ: We cannot face it / We have no power over it

ai.seo_question: What is the supplication for distress and fear of authorities in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith highlights the Ahl al-Bayt's strategic use of divine attributes—specifically Allah's pre-existence (Qabl al-Shay'), creative power (Mukawwin), and permanence (Baqa')—to seek relief from political oppression and personal distress. This supplication reflects the Shia tradition of combining theological affirmation with practical petition, emphasizing reliance on God's eternal nature during times of uncertainty.
